I am unable to prescribe an atonement for him.
One should not even mentally contemplate how an expiation might come to be;
furthermore, listen to another point: in some cases, a fracture of the *liṅga* occurs.

Someone may kill out of desirelessness, yet that is proclaimed as his settled doctrine; someone may be a bearer of a shaven head and a skull-topped staff, yet he is called a practitioner of the Great Vow.
In the left hand is a skull-cup, adorned with a rosary of rudrākṣa beads; there is a lotus-petal earring on the ear and moonlight upon the head.
One should adorn the hands and feet, and wear a beautiful girdle at the waist;
then, having requested permission from the Guru who acts as the preceptor (ācārya).
And one should observe such a vow while wandering upon the surface of the earth:
staying for one night in a village and likewise for three nights in a small town.
One should stay for five nights in a city, for seven nights in a great city,
or in a cremation ground, at a solitary linga, beneath a single tree, or at a crossroads.
In an empty house, on a riverbank, on a mountain, at a river mouth or the ocean,
in cremation grounds and other sacred fords, and always at the sacred sites of Rudra.
In these places, one should perform recitation (japa) as the basis for the purification of the body,
subsisting on vegetables, roots, and fruits, or even eating every other day.
Having killed one who is worthy of honor, whether he be a fellow-initiate (samayin), a spiritual son (putraka), or even [the master himself],
one should then recite ten koṭis [of mantras] and approach the guru once again.
One who has been initiated into the Bhairava sacrifice becomes pure through the purification of all objects;
liberated from all sins, he is purified—of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess, when a son has died, the recitation (japa) should be performed twofold;
when one who has committed a sin has died, the recitation should indeed be twice that amount.
And when the noble one has died, O Goddess, perform the recitation of "Kovāśī.
I shall perform the recitation; then, as before, he will be purified from his sins.
There is no doubt that one is purified here, even if the heart is defiled;
if one conceals [the transgression] out of delusion, one is purified by a single thousand [recitations].
As before, for those beginning with the "son" (putraka), it should be doubled and doubled again;
a fool who reviles his guru is purified by half a lakh [of repetitions].
But he who, during the fortnight of his Guru, steals his property, or where loss occurs, should recite one hundred thousand [mantras]; if he is devoid of wisdom, half of that.
O Goddess, he who hears slander of the Guru, does not go [to him], or does not show respect—he too is a traitor to the Guru; yet he becomes pure by reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times.
For even a courtesan who was enjoyed by his preceptor Śailarāja— alas, such was the hope of the disciple that he imagined her to be his wife.
In this case as well, one should recite it exactly one hundred thousand times; of this there is no doubt.
O beloved of the Guru, he who voids excrement or urine upon the bare ground [incurs this].
Neither a disciple nor [the teacher] himself should ever perform [this] in that place. Having performed [the rite] and recited the root mantra ten million times, one becomes purified.
When one sees the play of animals, one should recite [the mantra] a hundred times with desire;
likewise, when one has traveled a long distance and returned again.
Twenty thousand [verses] have been taught to the disciples, O lady of virtuous vows;
however, for one's own disciple, it is proclaimed that the number is double.
I shall now describe the fault of one who constantly maintains association with those who observe the Mahāvrata as well as with the Pāśupatas.
The practitioner of mantra should recite one hundred thousand times for the consumption of the *lakṣamanta* and other substances;
likewise for the Śvetārhats and the Buddhas, O Blessed One.
The fruit [of this] has already been declared as resulting from contact with and the consumption of [the substance],
as well as by Soma, Brahmā, Skanda, Viṣṇu, the Goddess, and the Mothers.
O Goddess, those priests who subsist by performing worship [for others] are indeed *devalakas*;
I shall now declare the expiation for them.
When a vessel made of clay has been touched after being placed together with things that cause defilement, one should discard it; this is the considered rule.
Iron, copper, brass, gold, silver, and so forth may be produced;
their purification occurs in fire, while the removal of impurities is accomplished with ash.
That which [is defiled] by conch shells, mother-of-pearl, and so forth, one should purify with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya);
cloth is purified by water, as is that which has been colored by mantra-water.
Likewise, one should sprinkle leather and other such items with water consecrated by mantras;
for wooden objects, washing is prescribed, while for beds and seats, sprinkling is taught.
Having thus understood the many [impurities] of the forest, one should indeed purify them;
when there is a desire for association or oneness with those who have abandoned birth.

O Goddess, one should recite it twenty thousand times; if free from desire, one should recite it one hundred thousand times, provided one has not understood the true nature of the scriptures and the compendium of the principles of knowledge.
If one performs the initiation out of delusion and subsequently performs it again,
one should recite five hundred thousand [mantras] there if one desires auspiciousness.
If one reveals knowledge, scripture, or mantra out of affection or greed,
the practitioner of mantra shall be purified by performing one hundred thousand recitations as an expiation.
O Goddess, when one steals a scripture, one should recite half of that [number];
likewise, when one breaks it, it is proclaimed that one should recite double [the number] for one who burns it.
But he who, out of greed for wealth, acts as a "kisser" after having discerned [the truth], should not do so even while knowing it; likewise, one should not disclose the reality.
Due to negligence on the part of the preceptors, they do not perform the fire-ritual (agnikārya) even after reciting the mantra six thousand times.
Within the rainy season, the ritual should be performed with a hundred thousand recitations;
one should place the seed-syllable at the rampart and the archway, and the cave-mantra in the cremation ground and the crossroads.
At a crossroads, at a triangular junction, in the middle of a river,
at a confluence, at a solitary tree, or likewise at a well— when the sequence of excreting feces and urine occurs there.
If unintentional, one should mutter the Ghoramantra two hundred times; if intentional, three hundred times.
In this way, for other types of offenses, purification occurs through the recitation of the Ghoramantra.
Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter on expiation in the *Sarvasvacchanda*, consisting of twelve thousand verses.
In the *Kāmikā* [Tantra], within the section on the descent of Brahmā (Brahmāvatāra), that which is called the *Kāmikā* expiation is written here:
having caused the death of either a lifelong celibate (*naiṣṭhika*) or a householder who is a teacher (*deśika*).
Relying upon the five groups of eight and a single linga with a serene mind,
one becomes purified after completing fifty thousand [recitations] and then ten lakhs.

If [the gift] is bestowed out of desire, it is [counted] by the number of atoms; if out of lack of desire, it is by the number of dust-particles. If it should be a thousandfold, this is so provided he is not turned away from the goal.
With his eyes covered by a cloth turned inside out, devoted to the Dharma,
he was smeared with ashes and killed by the Vināyakas.
For the purpose of determining the stability [of the image], one should have it made with a hundred-thousandth part [of the prescribed size];
then, having held that weapon, [one should bathe it] with water purified by a cloth.
The practitioner, joined with the conduct of the observance (samayācāra), having prepared the vessel,
should place Śiva in the cremation ground and sprinkle him with eight handfuls [of water].
O fair-faced one, with the letters beginning with *a* and ending with *ha*, together with the *dhuṭ* and *tuṣ*,
one should sprinkle [the disciple] with the Supreme Lord, who flashes forth in an instant.
And by knowledge, O Great Goddess, as well as by killing a practitioner of the observance (samayin) who is intent on the propitiation of the Guru through ignorance and a number of eight views;
Relying upon a great river, one should perform the sprinkling with four hundred thousand [repetitions];
up to ten days' interval, according to desire, by way of the number of hundred-thousands.
While the *pāśa* is being severed, one should sprinkle [the disciple] with the *kāraṇeśvara*;
then, while the *śakti* is being severed, the purification of the *pāśa* arises.

When a sin such as the killing of a Brahmin has occurred, it was previously declared that [the rite] should be performed with one's own chosen liṅgas; and if eight have been burnt through negligence, [the following applies].
The expiation for a mantra is one hundred thousand recitations and its re-ascension;
this applies even if it has fallen through negligence or has been touched.
Or one may desire the fundamental purificatory rite (saṃskāra) for the tenth time;
however, when the linga has fallen from the hand, purification occurs through fifty thousand [recitations].
When the linga is two cubits in height, [the purification is] with five *ayutas* in a pure place;
but when it has fallen due to negligence upon a linga that is two cubits [in height], [the purification is as follows].

If a *liṅga* that has not fallen from a person of ordinary stature is broken through negligence, its purification shall always consist of one hundred thousand [recitations], followed by the fundamental consecration (*saṃskāra*).
"O fair-faced one, the Blessed Lord Śiva has declared that there is an expiation for that [transgression] through the contemplation of the Śivaliṅga, the Sūtra, and the knowledge of Śiva."
If it is fallen, lost, destroyed, or burnt, one becomes pure by reciting the *lakṣa* [of mantras] one hundred thousand times;
likewise, there is purification through expiation (*prāyaścitta*) and re-installation.
Thus ends the expiation (prāyaścitta) as it appeared in response to a question in the Kāmika [Tantra], titled "The Inquiry in the Kāmika. || 35 ||
Now, in the *Siddhayogeśvarīmata*, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] division concerning the seed-syllables (*bījabheda*), the expiation (*prāyaścitta*) is written:
"O Goddess of Gods, all are purified; however, one whose *liṅga* is broken is not purified.
The *liṅga* is said to be of two kinds: the stationary (*sthāvara*) and likewise the mobile (*jaṅgama*)."
Even in the case of the punishment of women, the twofold action would not be purified.
O Goddess, when the body [of the image] is lost or ruined due to negligence or separation,
there should again be a propitiatory rite (*prāyaścitta*) of one hundred thousand [recitations].
When a mobile linga, O Goddess, has fallen and then been reinstalled...
Having performed one hundred and eight [recitations], one should perform the recitation fourfold.
If [the mantra] falls from the hand or is destroyed in five ways, one should indeed recite it sixfold.
Having understood this, the knower of mantras should perform the expiation.

And it has been said: "But when there is a difference regarding the seed—whether unintentionally or intentionally—the wise man should perform the penance bestowed by his guru or [prescribed] by himself."
If one associates with those who have cast off their veils, the recitation (japa) must be performed one hundred thousand times;
however, if one acts contrary to the prescribed conduct, the recitation must be performed five thousand times.
Having killed a woman through negligence, or having contracted a disease that obstructs [the senses],
one becomes pure by reciting the mantra five hundred thousand times or by performing the *lakṣahoma* sacrifice.
If a practitioner or an initiate should kill [an animal] through negligence,

he is purified by reciting one million mantras ten times over and offering one hundred thousand oblations for each million. If it was done intentionally, he is purified by ten million recitations and one million oblations.
One becomes purified through remorse by undertaking the vow of the skull;
and having killed a cow through negligence, one should perform the appropriate penance.
One should also dwell in solitude, be habituated to bathing three times a day,
and perform the recitation (japa) during the three junctions of the day, sequentially one hundred and eight times each.
Having remained established in the vow for six months, one should then feed those who observe the vow;
likewise, having intentionally killed [an animal], one should then feed those who observe the vow.
No expiation exists.
O Goddess, by selling liquor-vessels or even images of the deities,
one is purified by a hundred thousand [repetitions], and likewise by undergoing initiation once again.
O Goddess, having seen a woman naked with her breasts exposed through negligence, one should recite [the mantra] seven times; she shall be purified, without a doubt.
Thus ends the chapter on expiation (*prāyaścitta*) within the *Bījabheda* section of the *Siddhayogeśvarīmata*, consisting of twenty-four thousand verses. 36.
Now, in the Bhairavaśrotas, according to the Siddhayogeśvarīmata, within the Cūḍāmaṇi Tantra, the progressive expiation (prāyaścitta) is written.
The Goddess said:
O Great Lord, the expiation for one who, having understood the meaning of the scriptures and the lineage, violates the commitments (samaya) has been indicated in the root mantra.
O Lord of Gods, by what action would a man— whether he be a *samayin*, a son, or even a *sādhaka* or *ācārya*— become liable for expiation?
"By what action is one purified? Tell me how that is so, O Bhairava.
Bhairava said:
O Goddess, I have merely indicated it in the Root Tantra, but I have not fully explained it;
rather, the definitive determination of the expiation is found in the great tantra known as the Kalpa.
It is explained in brief out of a desire for the welfare of living beings:
if Śaṅkara, through delusion, becomes the discarded offering (nirmālya) for anyone;
By reciting [the mantra] one thousand times during the three junctions of the day for up to seven days until the end of the cutting [of the thread],
one is purified by means of the Vidyā known as Samaya.
One who eats the discarded offerings of desire for half a day or even for a full day is purified after six months by chanting [mantras] over her bones at their joints.
Whether intentionally or unintentionally, one who desires his own success should strive to avoid the remains of offerings (nirmālya) belonging to Śaṅkara.
One should consume [the offering] at a Bhairava-liṅga, whether it be mobile or immobile;
through one's own mantra, success is attained, otherwise Śaṅkara [himself] would become [the obstacle].
O Great Goddess, at the time of sacrifice during the sporting of the host of heroes,
Śaṅkara shall not be present there, nor whatever mantra is being worshipped.
Whether unintentionally or intentionally, by transgressing against his guru,
that evil-minded person falls into an evil state and becomes a fit recipient for penance.
And there shall be no success for him in this world or in the next;
therefore, Yama has prescribed that an expiation must be performed according to the Tantra.
By reciting this at the three junctions of the day for six months, one becomes purified;
O Goddess, this method, which is devoid of a fixed number of recitations, is prescribed for all cases.
But for one who violates the wife of a preceptor, a son of a preceptor, a daughter, or likewise a sister,
there is no atonement even in hundreds of millions of eons.
One should burn away the mental transgression against that teacher by remaining steadfast in the vow for one year and through the disciplined practice of recitation.
By that, his body shall become pure; otherwise, he would go to hell.
O Goddess, if the guru has fallen from his state, his accomplishment will certainly not occur.
All the deities are pleased, and he obtains the oral tradition;
but what can be said of one who, having failed to do so, violates the conduct of the samaya?
Having understood this, the wise man should carry out the command of his guru;
[he should do so] upon seeing a woman naked, her breasts exposed through negligence.
If the goddess pursues him, he is purified; there is no doubt about this. Whenever he sees the sport of animals, even if unintentionally, he should recite [the mantra] one hundred times.
O Goddess, regarding the consumption of meat and other such things forbidden in the Purāṇas,
one who is devoted to the practice of the path within the Samaya [tradition] [is not bound by them].
Because it functions in seven ways— whether through desire, lack of desire, or partial purity—
a certain person, being angry, speaks in contradiction with those who observe the commitments (samayins).
By reciting and practicing the mantra seven times in sequence at the three junctions of the day,
even if one is angry and speaks in opposition along with one's sons, [the result is achieved].
For two days, one should recite [the mantra] three times each day, with a number equal to that [of the previous count];
and together with the preceptors, one should say something regarding the form of the fire.
Whether one reviles Maheśa by speech or even by thought,
one becomes purified by remaining steadfast in the vow and reciting [the mantra] ten thousand times.
One should again ask for forgiveness; otherwise, O Goddess of the gods, that dull-witted person with an angry mind is not purified at all, even together with the practitioners.
One who is devoted to constant practice is purified by two hundred [repetitions].
Furthermore, regarding women, there are five [repetitions] for those born of illicit unions; for a mature woman, a young girl, or a maiden, [the number is likewise determined].
One should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times every day during the three sessions of meditation;
O Goddess, this very same rule applies to both the practitioner and the teacher.
O Goddess, the Śastra is of many kinds, consisting likewise of five currents:
the Gārūḍa, the Bhūta-mantra, the Siddhānta, the Vāma, and the Dakṣiṇa.
The mantras extracted from the Śāstras, such as the Tarjanī and Karaṇa-mantras,
as well as the Itihāsas, Purāṇas, and the Bhārata, shall exist in the future.
O Goddess, the entire ocean of scriptures emerged from the lotus-mouth of Śiva;
likewise, regarding the refutation of those scriptures consisting of the five streams.
While adorning oneself as a practitioner of the *samaya*, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times;
indeed, even if one has unintentionally committed some act that constitutes the fivefold impurity of a Śaiva.
O Goddess, if one who is established in the observances and firm in his vows should intentionally kill [a living being], even after reciting the mantra ten lakhs of times, no atonement exists.
But half [the merit] is gained by reciting half the mantra; likewise, through union with Śaṅkara,
one should recite five times upon being struck, and when blood is seen from a wound.
If the *liṅga* slips a distance of one cubit (*hasta*), one is purified by ten thousand recitations;
the measure of the recitation increases according to the same sequence.
The recitation should be performed at the three junctions of the day, increasing in sequence with the passing days;
having remained established in the vow for one month, one should then feed an image.
In the case of a daily rite, one is purified by a hundred [repetitions]; likewise for the omission of the twilight prayers (saṃdhyā).
For the killing of a Brāhmaṇa, one is purified from that state by fifty thousand [repetitions].
Purity is likewise proclaimed through supernatural power; the Buddhist naked ascetic is said to possess a twofold [purity].
Whether unintentionally or intentionally, no expiation is required.

Thus ends the chapter on expiation (prāyaścitta) in the Bhairava Garden, within the section on the Superior Knowledge in the *Cūḍāmaṇi Tantra*, which consists of three thousand five hundred verses and belongs to the *Siddhayogeśvarīmata* in the stream of Bhairava (*Bhairavastrota*).
Now, the expiation is written according to the Siddhayogeśvarīmata, in the twenty-four thousand [verse] work, the Trikasārottara.

Having committed the eating of what is not to be eaten, as well as the drinking of what is not to be drunk, and sexual intercourse—even with one who should not be approached—one is purified by a single recitation; for approaching those who must not be approached, by two.
O Goddess, by reciting [the mantra] three times upon touching a Mleccha or similar person, one is liberated;
by a thousand recitations, one may purify even the killing of a cow or the killing of a Brahmin.
In the event of killing a woman, sexual intercourse, as well as in the case of a change of gender,
and when the twilight prayers (saṃdhyā) have been omitted, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times.
O Goddess, one should purify the property of the gods with five thousand [repetitions];
even after committing the slaughter of all living beings and killing everything moving and stationary.
By reciting it exactly one hundred and eight times, one is liberated from all sins;
in the case of a bad dream, it should be chanted three times, and in the case of a portentous omen, four times.
The practitioner should perform the rite of expiation (niṣidhā) on his foot and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times,
even when striking a woman or a child, or when speaking harsh words.
By reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, one is liberated from all sins;
however, if the practitioner has come into contact with another practitioner, he should recite it one thousand times.
One should avoid contact with others who observe different vows;
however, if someone should by mistake recite [the mantra] five thousand times, it shall be divided into five parts.
By ten thousand [recitations], the purification of all transgressions occurs;
even one who has committed every sin is purified when weighed on the scales.
By ten thousand recitations and fire oblations, one is liberated from the five great sins;
if one studies the scripture on a day when study is forbidden, one should perform one thousand and eight recitations.
Whatever sin has been accumulated through desire or even through lack of desire,
it is not equal to a single [sin] of one who is free from desire before bathing in Kāśī.
O Bhairavī, that lustful one is completely liberated by twenty-five thousand [recitations];
therefore, I shall now declare the vidyā for the purpose of expiation.
Oṃ aghore hrīṃ paramaghore hūṃ ghorarūpe haḥ ghoghoramukhi bhīmabhīṣaṇe ca māpi vahe ruru ra ra phaṭ phaṭ hreṃ haḥ phaṭ.
The Vidyā known as Parāparā, which destroys all sins,
has been extracted at the end of the divine division by means of forty-one syllables.
Thus ends the chapter on expiation in the *Siddhayogeśvarīmata*, within the twenty-four thousand [verse] work known as the *Trikasārottara*. 38.
In this great ocean of all-knowledge, the rite of expiation is now set forth:
the killing of a Brahmin, the drinking of intoxicants, the slaughter of a cow, and the reviling of one's guru.
Having come into contact with the touch of a Caṇḍāla, having killed a living being,
or having eaten food that is unfit to be eaten, one is purified immediately upon the birth of a son.
O Goddess, one who delights in consuming feces and urine, or in eating beef,
becomes purified by the Vāmadeva mantra after committing an act of incest.

In eating the remains of offerings (nirmālya), in consuming food-leavings, or even in touching those who have consumed leavings; likewise, in the failure of a vow, in the abandonment of a vow, and in transgressing the command of the Guru.
For cutting down the trees of merit, as well as for stepping over the remains of offerings (nirmālya),
and likewise for [insulting] a bearer of the Liṅga (liṅgin), one is purified by the Aghora mantra alone.
One who causes abortion, a traitor to his guru, a slayer of women, a seller of women,
one who betrays a friend, and a reviler of gods and brahmins.
He who initiates out of greed for wealth and he who performs an installation ceremony,
as well as one who eats the food of a woman in her menses, is purified by the recitation of the Vaktra-mantra.
O Goddess, by the recitation of this mantra, a person destroys all that has been proclaimed as the impurity of verbal, mental, and physical actions.
For in this way, O beloved, all that is born of action— whether auspicious or inauspicious—
one should destroy the inauspicious by relying upon auspicious action.
Birth, death, old age, disease, suffering, and grief are inextricably linked; through recitation and burnt offerings one overcomes them. Therefore, perform the meritorious recitation.
Through recitation, sin is purified; through recitation, one obtains anointing. Whether it be a bad dream or an impending misfortune, it is destroyed by the merit arising from recitation.
One should always perform meritorious deeds; through merit one shall obtain happiness.
Therefore, [strive for] happiness.
Therefore, having become full of merit, one should perform meritorious deeds;
and having understood the duties according to their divisions, one should act as a teacher, a youth, or an elder.
An expiation must indeed be granted as prescribed in the scriptures and spoken by the Guru;
for the word of the Guru is authoritative, and it has been spoken by me.
Thus ends the section on expiation in the *Sarvajñānamahodadhi*. || 39 ||
Now, the expiation for the unauthorized consumption of mercury (rasa) in the *Sāhasra* [section] is written:
O lady of excellent complexion, if the property of the gods has been consumed even unintentionally.
One is purified by reciting the Bahurūpa mantra ten million times; for intentional acts, the recitation must be doubled, and purification occurs through re-initiation.
Alternatively, one should cause the remains of the offerings to Śiva (śivanirmālya) or the drainage water (praṇāla) to be swallowed;
having recited [the mantra] thirty thousand times and offered eight hundred jars of water.
In that case, purification from intentional [consumption] occurs after two tens of thousands [of breaths]; from unintentional [consumption], after twenty thousand;
and when fire or substances have ever been consumed unintentionally, [the same applies].

The practitioner of mantra should perform one hundred thousand recitations; however, if he does so out of desire, he should perform one million. Furthermore, if he unintentionally consumes forbidden substances, he should perform one million recitations.
By means of which two hundred thousand [recitations], one becomes pure again through initiation from desire;
[this applies] regarding the property of the deity, the property of the Guru, and the property of Caṇḍeśvara.
Having observed a fast for three nights, the wise man should recite the mantra,
O Lord of the Gods, by whom the remains of the offering were consumed even against his will.
Having recited fifty thousand times, one is purified; there is no doubt about this.
For the Bahurūpa mantra, one should recite twice as many times if so desired.
Those whose origin is seen to be from the root of Śaṅkara’s station are to be known as heavy,
heavier, or likewise very light.
O beloved, those faults regarding divine substances and the like that were described by me,
as well as those arising from contact with them, have been explained in the context of contact.
The illustrious one is proclaimed as the third portion of the *saṅkara*;
he is to be recited externally, whether unintentionally or intentionally.
In contact with those who are auspicious, one becomes auspicious in turn; furthermore, the recitation (*japa*) of the *Śaṅkara* [mantra] therein has been described by me as being half [the length].
Thus ends this expiation in the sixth thousand [verses] of the Rasacchanda. || 39 ||
The expiation for Picumata is now written down.
One who has killed a Brahmin, remaining firm in his vows and well-composed, should mutter [the mantra] one hundred thousand times;
so too one who has struck a Linga, whether it be fixed or known as "living."
One who is endowed with the five-fold austerity should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times;
having cut off his ear and other [limbs], he shall become capable of performing ten lakh recitations.
Eating only at night and endowed with the five-fold heat (pañcātapas), one should perform recitation;
O Goddess of the Gods, if the *ikṣusūtra* is lost, the recitation consists of ten thousand repetitions.
When it has been burnt and purified by a hundred thousand recitations (lakṣajapa) performed ten times,
then the mantras placed within the city [of the body] will not release their defects.
Thus ends the section on expiation in the Picumata. || 40 ||
In the Pārameśvara Mahātantra, the expiation is written:
having eaten in the context of [initiating] pregnant women, one should recollect the Vāmanu mantra.
In the rite of arranging the hair, one should meditate upon Sadyojāta;
from the time of emerging [from the womb] until reaching the seat, one should practice the meditation on Puruṣendra.
And having eaten at the ceremony of tonsure, as well as at the piercing of the ears,
and likewise at the vow and the gift of a cow, one may eat without hesitation.
In the case of marriage, however, whatever may be the limit, no fault exists therein;
but having eaten at the fourth meal-time, one should remember the Vāmadeva hymn.
One should indeed eat at *pākayajñas* and *haviryajñas*;
one should also eat at the *saumasaṃsthās*, for that is remembered as the limit of purification.
Furthermore, when constructing wells, ponds, or gardens,
or during the consecration ceremonies (*pratiṣṭhā*) of deities, one must never eat [at such times].
Upon both birth-impurity and death-impurity, having eaten, one should remember Vāma;
likewise, one should not eat even at one's own home during birth-impurity or death-impurity.
Having practiced this for three nights, one who has consumed [forbidden food] becomes purified;
furthermore, even those of the four castes who have been suspected may eat until the end of the initiation ceremony.
One may eat from the three castes beginning with the Brāhmaṇa who have been consecrated for a sacrifice and remain established in their own duties, but never from Śūdras.
In the absence of others, Śūdras who are endowed with purity and proper conduct,
as well as those Śūdras who are devoted [to the teacher], are declared to be those whose food may be eaten.
Only two types of ascetics are to be fed: the celibate student (brahmacārī) and likewise the householder (gṛhastha).
Their wealth is not to be consumed, nor indeed that of those who bear other sectarian marks (anyaliṅgin).

For all those whose minds have been stilled, the recitation (japa) of all [mantras] everywhere should be performed while standing in water up to the neck, with the senses restrained according to the rule.
"In this way, there is indeed purification for one who possesses the word of the Guru.
Thus ends the chapter on "The Food of a Pregnant Woman" in the General Section of the *Pārameśvara Mahātantra*. || 42 ||
Now, the expiation (*prāyaścitta*) is written in the *Āgneyamahātantra*, the *Mohacūrottara*:
"O Lord of Śacī, I shall now proclaim the expiation to you."
For the sake of removing defects and for the further establishment of Dharma,
even though Janārdana was not asleep, [this was done] either out of delusion or ignorance.
He who causes the *pavitra* to be made while being a sinner deluded by sin,
shall remove [his sin] by fasting for five days and reciting the mantra fifty thousand times.
One should thus attain purity; however, one should never perform it after the month of Bhādrapada, for in the Siddhānta, one would become a partaker of fault.

Having recited [the mantra] two hundred thousand times with intensity, he becomes purified even of that which was committed during the three months beginning with Āṣāḍha, whether by chance or through ignorance.
In that regard also, O Purandara, the prescribed atonement is as follows:
constant adherence to one's own scriptures and the observance of the conduct of the covenant.
Having thoroughly examined it, one should practice the avoidance of prohibited conduct,
exactly as it has been heard, exactly as it has been seen, and exactly as taught by the masters who bring about cessation.
Transgressing that [rule] by contradicting one's own established doctrine,
if the twilight prayer (saṃdhyā) is omitted even once, one should mutter [the mantra] a hundred times while remaining unborn (ajātasya).
If one intentionally omits all three daily rites, the penance is threefold along with a fast; if one omits a single rite while asleep, one should recite the *dakṣiṇa* mantra a thousand times.
Whether once, twice, thrice, or at midnight,
one should observe the fast with full devotion when a lapse in ritual action has occurred.
One who omits [the recitation] at the proper time for the sake of the gods or for the sake of the guru incurs sin;
likewise, wherever there is censure of the scriptures or censure of the guru, or where [censure of] the *liṅgas* occurs, [one incurs sin].
Therefore, one should depart far from that place and recite the *sadyojāta* mantra a hundred times;
this applies to those joined with great sins as well as others who perform evil deeds.
Those who have fallen [from their caste] and those who are accused should be avoided with great effort;
however, if one performs the oblation out of ignorance, he should recite the mantra ten thousand times facing the south.
One should not step on the shadow of a guru, nor that of Śiva, nor of those who bear the sectarian marks (liṅgin).
Having recited the Rūpiṇī mantra three hundred times, he becomes equal to a hundred Brahmins and a hundred virgins.
If a thousand [transgressions] have occurred when the *liṅga* was overturned, one becomes pure by performing twice that number;
if it was overturned three or four times, by ten thousand; and if it fell into a chasm, by one hundred thousand.
In the case of a blow from a mallet or similar object, [the distance] is two myriads (20,000) from the light leaf;
for praise and so forth, it is within the house; and upon contact with the right [hand], it is three myriads (30,000).
If the installed liṅga is stolen, lost, or consumed by fire through negligence,
one becomes pure by installing a new one of that same form after reciting the Ghoramantra one hundred thousand times.
If the *liṅga* falls upon its support, one should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times for each *tāla*;
however, if it falls without a support, the recitation should be double that amount, whether the duration be less or more than a *kalpa*.
But for an offense regarding the rosary, the wise man should perform the penance prescribed for a quarter [of the sin];
likewise in the case of not returning the vessel, or its breaking, or its being turned over.
For one of impure mind, purification is said by their respective lords to be two hundred up to one thousand, or half of that;
on a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), they say the penance is double.
Having fasted for three nights before that auspicious fire of Nirvāṇa and having recited the Rūpin mantra ten thousand times, he attains purification without a doubt.
For even when Nirvana has been protected, the practitioner, having fasted for a day and night and having recited [the mantra] a thousand times in many forms, becomes purified.
Having completed the forenoon and midday [rituals],
one who desires both worldly enjoyment and liberation should wander for alms (*mādhukarī*) while maintaining the body in its natural state.
Having caused that alms-food to be recited over, he should wait a short while and then depart elsewhere;
he should wander for alms without turning back, having ascertained the conduct and the status of the members of the [four] classes.
Having placed it in a clean spot, one should attain a state of purity equal to that of the pure;
then, having thoroughly cleansed the feet with earth and washed the hands, one should thereafter sip water.
Then, having performed the ash-bath (bhasmasnāna), one should also recollect the two mantras;
having meditated upon the Astra-mantra as a flaming torch, one should look around and dispel all fear.
Having offered it to his preceptor for the sake of Śiva, he should eat according to the prescribed rite;
then, having sipped water as before and bathed, he should remember and bow to Śiva and his preceptor.
Having established his residence with unasked-for gifts or with his own wealth inherited through tradition,
he should, upon being touched by one initiated in his own caste, bathe, sip water, and recite [the mantra] one hundred times.
If that [water] is touched by those who have not been initiated, one should bathe, sip water, and recite [the mantra] a hundred times;
if it is touched by those who have been initiated in its vicinity, one should bathe, sip water, and recite it two hundred times.
If that [water] is touched by one who is not initiated, it is prescribed that one should perform recitation (japa) while fasting.
Having understood this, others should act accordingly, omitting one quarter [of the penance].

For a man, the impurity lasts for three nights for those born from the Aghora, Vāma, Jāti, and Īśa [faces], starting from the Brāhmaṇa and so forth; however, he becomes pure by touching one born from the Aghora face after ten thousand [repetitions of the mantra].
O Śakra, lord of the gods, one should prescribe the *sakṛcchra* penance thirty thousand times for touching a Caṇḍāla;
O lord of the gods, once this is known, no further expiation need be performed here.
If one unintentionally eats food that has been touched by liquor,
or food that has been touched by feces, urine, or semen, or food that has been licked by crows or dogs;
[Food] defiled by monkeys, crocodiles, jackals, crows, boars, and pigs; or that which has been touched by a Śūdra or by those of the lowest castes while he is impure from eating remnants.
Having performed his bath and remaining without food, he should consume the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) at the shrine of Kipigrahāśilādakṣa.
Thus, with a concentrated mind, he should recite the Ghoramantra one thousand times during the twilight ritual.
For three days he should eat only at night, bathe with water, and remain intent on meditation.
On the fourth day, one should perform a thousand oblations for the beloved deity;
then, by fasting, eating only at night, and consuming the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), one becomes purified.
A Kṣatriya, however, should prescribe purification for one intent on meditation;
for a Vaiśya, bathing at the three times of day; and for a Śūdra, one should prescribe the Sat-kṛcchra penance.
For all these, it is proclaimed that the penance is double if committed intentionally compared to unintentionally.
Having abandoned meat produced from impure substances, one should perform the *nirasana* for three days;
likewise for the *matsya*, *kaṇḍūka*, *sāmbuka*, *nasya*, and *kaparddikā*.
Having drunk water from a single source, the practitioner of mantras, observing a fast with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya),
is purified by vomiting after consuming food mixed with worms and insects.

Having discarded a small amount of rice that has been defiled by birds, hair, or insects, and having sprinkled with water what remains after it has been touched by ashes, the remainder may be eaten; it does not become impure.
If one should, through negligence, drink water that remains after being sipped,
he becomes pure by fasting for one night and consuming the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
Drinking this while falling into a snake, one goes to its end, deluded;
by reciting the Rūpiṇī-mantra a thousand times, one is purified with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
If one eats while having feces stuck to the anus, it is taught that he is impure;
first there must be purification, then a bath, and after sipping water (ācamana), he should perform the excellent rinsing.
Having recited [the mantra] one thousand times with a physical form, one becomes purified while observing a fast;
yet if one drinks water or eats food without having sipped water for purification, or performs the ritual recitation [in such a state], [one is not purified].
Even after reciting [the mantra] while fasting, one who has consumed the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) is not purified if the practitioner,
while still half-full from food, is defiled by excrement, liquor, or similar substances.
Even the terrible sin of associating with a woman is purified by the consumption of the five products of the cow (pañcagavya),
as is the case when a man drinks or eats without wearing his sacred thread (yajñopavīta).

One who has fasted and recited the *ghora* mantra becomes purified by consuming the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). However, when one is defiled by food remnants or touched by those who have food remnants on them, such as bamboo-workers and the like—
One becomes pure through bathing, purification, fasting, the consumption of the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), and the recitation of mantras;
this applies even to those who have touched bell-metal, copper, iron, silver, or lead.
Just as the purification of ashes by water was determined by Hara,
so too is the purification of conch shells, mother-of-pearl, and oyster shells desired to be like that of radiant substances.
It is said that milk is purified; this is declared to be the purification of curd. Having held it within the pressing of the curd, one should examine it immediately thereafter.
Curd is purified by sprinkling it with water when free from the impurity of food and the like;
likewise, the purification of well-heated clarified butter that has been boiled is proclaimed.

In this way, honey, jaggery, and the like are purified by sprinkling and contact with fire; likewise, vessels containing cooked grain are purified by thorough scrubbing, as are those that have been tasted or smeared.

A vessel that has been defiled by contact with food is purified by sprinkling; one contaminated by honey is purified by wiping; one defiled by the remnants of food is purified by cow-dung; and one defiled by impure substances is purified by its previous consecration.
O Pākaśāsana, I shall now briefly describe another pure internal [method]:
having bathed well and performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), the man becomes pure or clean.
Daily purification is required for those garments used by the ancestors and the gods;
one should discard the lower garment and the upper covering upon the occurrence of thunder.
A cloth washed by a washerman becomes pure even when washed again;
for garments dyed with leather, purification is achieved with alkaline water.
Silken garments are purified by *ambikā* and *urukṣa*; linen cloths by white mustard seeds;
woolen cloths by *śrīphala* fruits; and blankets made of animal hair by *ariṣṭaka* fruits.
Indeed, all things such as grass and wood become pure simply by sprinkling;
for those items that are already pure but are gathered together, purification is held to occur through sprinkling.
If among many things gathered together, anything is defiled by an impurity, one should remove that [defiled item], such as grass and so forth, and purify the rest so that it becomes clean.
O Purandara, behold the pure substance in the artisan’s hand extended;
there is purity through the washing of fruits, free from fault.
A Brahmin is purified after ten days; a king (Kṣatriya) after twelve days;
a Vaiśya after fifteen days; and the purification for a Śūdra takes one month.
O Purandara, that twice-born man who possesses only his caste but lacks the performance of religious rites,
yet is endowed with the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences and has maintained the sacred fires, is truly a Brahmin.
One is purified at that very moment by bathing; having understood this, one should apply it elsewhere.
Those who are truthful, of noble birth, and always devoted to dharma—p. 51a)—[are thus purified].
Śūdra women become pure in a fortnight; there is no need for further deliberation on this point. Indeed, four types of women may always be wedded by a Brāhmaṇa.
The period of birth-impurity for those [women] lasts ten, six, two, and one day respectively;
it is purified by the second [rite]. There is no increase [in the duration] due to a subsequent birth, nor does a corpse [impurity] extend over [an existing] impurity.
For those who possess spiritual power, there is no birth-impurity (sūtaka) when entering a cremation fire;
nor is there birth-impurity for kings, artisans, or female slaves.

In the case of a corpse, however, one should perform the ritual separately; one should not join it with those [other corpses]. If that [corpse] is not abandoned, then purification will not occur for those born of that lineage.
O Lord, one is purified by bathing after the disclosure of a full pregnancy;
whether the child is born alive, or if it is known to have been stillborn, or even if it is born [later].
Or rather, she should not perform purification; [instead] she should observe [the rules]:
until the teeth are born, it is immediate; for one day after the teeth have emerged.

For the Cūḍā ceremony, it is declared that the period is three days; in that case, there is no increase beyond that due to the vow. Beyond this, purification is as previously stated; this is the rule for all castes.
The fine for an unmarried girl who has reached puberty shall be double;
this same rule is to be understood to apply to female relatives such as a mother-in-law, and also to a maternal uncle’s son.
If one is in another country and the funeral cake is offered separately, the bath should be performed without that [specific] guru;
this applies to those for whom the state of being a bound soul (paśutva) has been removed by means of the perfect initiation of liberation (nirvāṇadīkṣā).
For one who is devoid of such contact, there would be no impurity of death or birth;
therefore, even when impurity from birth exists, Śakra is to be worshipped by others.

A householder should always avoid eating the food of others, performing services for others at night, and all such activities that involve dependence on others. He should constantly perform his own duties.
With substances previously intended for the purpose, even during periods of birth-impurity or death-impurity,
worship for the sake of Dharma must be performed by those initiated, as well as by others who have undertaken the vow.

Without performing separate cooking for themselves, those who follow the worldly initiation should perform the internal sacrifice (antaryāga) as well as the rites of recitation, ritual bathing, and so forth.
Having prescribed the penance, there is no other way for the state [of the disciple] to be determined;
for one who conducts himself in this manner, the threefold accomplishment is not far off.
O performer of a hundred sacrifices, upon seeing a bad dream, one should perform this rite of release.

Having recited the Aghora mantra one hundred and eight times and likewise addressed the lowest [of the low], he is purified by water alone; however, that which ends in a smear must be cleansed with earth and water.

If the property of a deity, a teacher, or a guru has been consumed by someone today, then one hundred thousand pādas must be paid; for a lifelong student (naiṣṭhika), it is held that double should be given.
Then, having stepped upon the discarded flower offering (*sunirmālya*), one should mutter [the mantra] five hundred times;
it should be known that if done out of desire, it is threefold, accompanied by the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*).
That which has been touched by the *nirmālya* (remains of offerings) is then called *hāropa*;
however, the *nirmālya* that is deficient by one-eighth [of its qualities] results from the transgression of giving it away or consuming it.

He who steps over the remains of offerings (nirmālya), or even gives them away out of ignorance, should mutter the *Ghoramantra* ten thousand times; likewise for one who violates the rules of conduct or the sacred scriptures.
Upon touching the remains of offerings (nirmālya), one must discard merchandise, medicinal herbs,
water that has undergone transformation, as well as sugarcane, asafoetida, and cumin.
Saindhava and the rest, along with camphor; Kaṭuka and the rest, along with *vraṇula*; as well as sandalwood ash, bamboo, clay, and wood.
It is taught that all things, such as grain and so forth, must be abandoned; one who has gone abroad remains pure.
In this way, it should be understood in other cases as well, having discerned the relative strength or weakness of the substances.
The wise person should always purify; for as long as one is not pure, bondage is certain. He who desires liberation quickly must resolve to achieve purity.
For one who is established in pure devotion, neither spiritual perfection nor liberation is far off;
this applies whether one is eighty years of age or even a child not yet sixteen.
Women, or those afflicted by disease, deserve only half of the penance;
even in those cases, having considered their suffering, one should prescribe half of that half.
One who is unable to perform it himself due to being twice as deluded [by passion] becomes pure by bathing after reciting the mantra one hundred and fifty times.
At night, fasting until the fifth watch, he performed thirty thousand recitations; thereafter, by way of increase, he doubled that number.
But the conjunction is half of that, and half of that again is in Śaṅkara.
[One should consider] place, time, age, power, caste, devotion, and the sequence of actions.
O noble Purandara, this most wonderful gift should be bestowed; fasting is not for one afflicted by illness, nor for those of good conduct whose minds are solely intent on Śiva.
The expiation has been fully declared for those whose minds abide in the conduct not previously mentioned;
it extends over seventy million verses, O you who are the essence of the destroyer of delusion.
O lady of excellent vows, having extracted the essence, the *Lakṣagrantha* has been explained;
now, O leader of the gods, I have been touched upon by you once more in brief.
O Hari, that was declared by me, Mohacūḍa, with half of that [number],
and at its conclusion, with thousands of the essence of accomplishments (siddhisāra) equal to twice the moon.
This supreme scripture, endowed with the knowledge of yoga and other [attainments], has been explained;
it is a most excellent tantra of consecration, both very concise and profoundly deep.
That which increases the fourfold sphere of activity is further renowned as the supreme;
it should not be given to wicked beings who follow after censure.
O Purandara, [this applies] to those who hate their gurus and gods, as well as those who hate their preceptors and others,
and likewise whatever other wicked beings there may be.
Their scripture must always be kept secret; otherwise, there is an expiation.
[However, it may be given] to one who is devoted to the guru, the gods, and the sacred fire, who is pure, and firm in his vows.
"To him this scripture should be given," so said the Blessed Lord Śiva.
Thus ends the *Mohacūrottara* within the *Pratiṣṭhātantra*, which is part of the great *Āgneya-tantra*. || 43 ||
Alternatively, the chapter on expiation (prāyaścitta) from the Āthula [Tantra] is now written.
Īśvara said:
Those practitioners established on the path who have abandoned the proper conduct fall downward;
therefore, one must observe the conduct spoken by Śiva.
If one has incurred a fault through fate, passion, or likewise through delusion,
[the remedy is] bathing, recitation, fasting, burnt offerings, and indeed water-pots.
The offering of the seat of the five products of the cow destroys impurities and misdeeds;
likewise, it removes all diseases from the body as well as the fear of kings and thieves.
Likewise, in the event of danger from fire or water, as well as during the consumption of food from a woman in childbirth,
and in the performance of rites for one's guru, deities, or the sacred fire, the constant omission [of other duties] does not entail fault.
One should always, for as long as one lives, cause the ritual assemblies to be performed;
likewise, O dear child, a son must never act with disrespect at any time.
O Lord, the practitioner should always strictly avoid [disrespect] toward the Guru;
for he who recites the mantra during ritual action is to be worshipped by the disciple with devotion.
He who, through negligence, should join even a single lunar mansion with the southern [node],
is a member of the Kula, a performer of rites, and always devoted to the scriptures.
Exclusively devoted to the pure path, avoiding the wives of others,
proficient in the observances of his science, skillful, and free from hypocrisy and deceit.
One who is constantly devoted to the practice of yoga, who avoids harming living beings,
and who is free from speaking ill of others— such a person is remembered as a true Guru.
Whether a householder or a celibate student, one subject to penance is established in two ways;
each of these is to be known as twofold, according to the distinction between being unintentional or intentional.
In the case of women who are free from desire, one should prescribe double the purification for those who possess desire;
indeed, the purification for one with desire should be the same as that for a materialist.
I offer this oblation to the one who is free from desire and established in the final goal.
When the sun has entered the weapon (the western horizon), one should avoid performing worship during that portion of time,
O child, except during a lunar eclipse, as well as among practitioners.
If there is an omission of worship for one day, one should recite the fifth [mantra] a thousand times;
if it occurs through negligence or unintentionally, one becomes pure by this, but if intentionally, by double that amount.
For those who observe the fast and perform worship three times a day, or even once a month;
The expiation for these is equal; it is never less nor more in any case.
For those who perform worship at the three times of day, the omission of the specific time [of worship] constitutes a transgression.
As previously stated, purification must be performed by giving [the prescribed gift] and not otherwise;
in this very manner, one should prescribe the purification for perpetual celibates (naiṣṭhika) through the offering of a gift.

Due to fate, disease, delusion, fear of thieves, kings, and so forth—because of these defects, there is no state of being a "kāmin" (one who acts from desire); the remainder should be understood as arising from desire (kāma).
Starting from a single day up to a period of five days,
one should increase the number of oblations (homa) and ritual vessels (gaḍuka) by three hundred each day, as prescribed.
O child, if one part of a fortnight is omitted, one should recite twenty thousand [mantras] in the south;
if a month is omitted, however, one should double that and increase it by twenty thousand thereafter.
O Mahāsena, month after month, up until the end of the year, one should perform [the rite] as if it were constant; however, in the event of an omission, one should prescribe an expiation.

Whatever worship, recitation, fire-oblation, or other rites are performed on the eighth day and so forth with a desire for results, that merit is quadrupled; however, upon its omission, one becomes pure by performing a hundred repetitions of the Sadyojāta mantra.
If the three daily rites are omitted, it is held that the recitation (japa) must be performed with three times the merit and accompanied by fasting;
this is declared for unintentional omission, whereas for intentional omission, one should perform twice the penance.
For one who lives for material ends, it is declared to be twofold; for one established in the final stage of life, it is considered fourfold; and for a celibate student, it is said to be eightfold.
In the case of a lapse lasting many days, the previously mentioned penalty shall be sixfold;
however, if one is ill and deprived of fasting, that recitation is considered valid.
Since it is extremely difficult to perform oneself, and since the merit is doubled when done by another,
those initiated into the stream [of the teaching] should perform the expiation through others.

For the sake of achieving general success and for protection, as well as in matters such as expiatory rites, one's own mantra should not be employed; purification occurs after a thousand [recitations], and not otherwise.
One should avoid the *Garuḍāmbhūta-tantra* out of greed or affection; yet he who practices it through negligence is purified by hundreds of *vahurūpa* [mantras].
Those who revile the guru among the initiates, spiritual sons, and others,
should depart far from that place and recite the *sadyojāta* mantra a hundred times.
One must not commit adultery through action, mind, or speech;
if one should practice it out of delusion, purification is achieved by half a *lakṣa* and a quarter.
For maidens, the penance should be double, as it is when the offense is committed against other castes.
[The four mortal sins are] killing a Brahmin, drinking liquor, theft, and violating the teacher’s wife.
Regarding the connection with specific grave sins, five [penances] are prescribed;
having killed a twice-born man out of desire, one should always recite [the mantra] while standing in a cow-pen.
Having drunk liquor out of desire, one should always recite [the mantra] on the left side of Śiva’s temple;
having eaten milk-rice out of desire, one should recite it even in a terrible cremation ground.

Having committed the offense of approaching the teacher's wife, or through negligence having approached a man in the forest, one should perform yoga with all [the deities] and recite the fifth mantra on a mountain peak.
In the *Prakāśa*, one is purified by reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times intentionally;
in the case of a secret [transgression], purification is held to occur through one thousand recitations unintentionally.
If it is done intentionally and in secret, there shall be twenty thousand [strokes];
if unintentionally and in secret, there too shall be twenty thousand.
Except in the case of treachery against the guru, there is no purification for intentional [offenses];
rather, one must perform the Cāndrāyaṇa, Parāka, or Kṛcchra penances respectively.

I shall now fully describe the characteristics of the *taptakṛcchra* and *kṛcchra* penances for the five [sins] beginning with the killing of a Brahmin, as well as those of the *cāndrāyaṇa* and other rites, in their proper order.

One should observe eating a single meal for three days, and likewise for three days one should eat only what is gathered by hand; having eaten only at night for three days, one should subsist on air for three days.
This is declared to be the Kṛcchra penance originating from the Prājāpatya;
for three days one subsists on water alone, and for three days one's meal consists of milk.
When one drinks hot ghee for three days and then [fasts] for three days while consuming only water, that is declared the *taptakṛcchra*; now hear about the *atikṛcchra*.
The drinking of three palas of milk for twenty-one days,
according to this sequential method, is declared to be the Kṛcchra penance.
Atikṛcchra is fully described, and Parāka is now declared:
one who remains without food for twelve days is known as having performed the Parāka.
The increase of morsels by one per day for half a month occurs during the bright fortnight, and one should decrease them during the dark fortnight;
this is declared to be the procedure for Cāndrāyaṇa, which, O Lord, consists of water and is of the nature of water.
If Śūdras who have been initiated drink liquor,
purification occurs again through ten thousand repetitions of the Aghora mantra and the performance of the Kṛcchra penance.
Where is liquor and where is devotion to Śiva? Where is meat and where is the worship of Bhava? For those engaged in liquor and meat, O Śaṅkara, [the goal] remains far away.
And approaching the wife of one's guru—these four are equal [in gravity]. Indeed, in whatever house those who have unknowingly killed a cow may be present, [it becomes impure].
Purification from [the sin of] abandoning all one's belongings comes through the Kṛcchra penance and not otherwise;
likewise, having eaten out of desire, one becomes pure only after the Tapta-kṛcchra.

If one has eaten out of desire even once, purification comes through the Kṛcchra or Atikṛcchra penances; one should recite the Vāmadeva hymn for purification, while for eating at the end of a Parāka fast, the Parāka vow is prescribed.
Having realized this, or having consumed it, he would then become equal to that [wind].
By chance, she remained for a day with the washerwoman's black hide.
Purity is always attained by discarding the vessel; after three days, or from the fifth day thereafter, when he has eaten out of desire, or for Kṛṣṇā, it is through three days of intense recitation.
This [penance] is considered double for intentional [repetition], and half for a single instance of union;
for unintentional [repetition] over many watches of the night, one becomes pure through the Cāndrāyaṇa.

Whether due to desire or excessive attachment, he may indeed assume a form characterized by violence toward living beings; yet, through the recitation of the hundred-fold terrible mantra, he becomes pure.
If one who has been initiated is touched by someone of his own caste, he then becomes impure after sipping water;
having sipped water, even the initiated person should mutter the mantra of his own clan-lord one hundred times.
If one is touched by someone who has been initiated nearby, the expiation is as before;
if one is touched by someone who has not been initiated, one should bathe and recite [the mantra] three hundred times.
In the same way, for one who has been initiated and is crossing [a river],
if there is contact within three hundred [steps], that goat shall remain fasting.
In the same way, from touching one known as a Śūdra, and from touching one who has not been initiated,
even though he has been initiated, one must fast for two days for each thousand [verses].
Others perform a penance that is deficient by one quarter;
whether they be men, women, or mothers, the lords of their respective castes have declared this according to the Brāhmaṇas.

One becomes pure after three nights from touching an Aghora-mantra practitioner; for touching a Ghoramantra practitioner, one should recite the mantra ten thousand times; and for touching a Caṇḍāla, one should recite it thirty thousand times as a Kṛcchra penance.
O Six-faced One, having understood each time according to the contact, such is the expiation for him;
whereas for one who acts without knowing, it is a portion [of that], once he has subsequently come to know.
Furthermore, [food] touched by mantras and the like, or by liquor and such things,
or by semen, urine, or feces, or that which has been pecked at by a crow— [is unfit].
If it has been touched by village pigs, vultures, jackals, monkeys, or cocks, or even by a non-Aryan, or if it is defiled by the remnants of food from a Śūdra or others;
Having bathed and observed a fast for a day and night, one should consume the five products of the cow (pañcagavya);
furthermore, at each twilight, one should practice the recitation of the thirty-two-syllable mantra a thousand times.
For three days, one should eat only at night, refrain from bathing, and remain intent on meditation;
then, on the fourth day, one should perform a thousand oblations (homa) to the chosen deity.
Just as one who eats at night is purified by eating only once before dawn,
so too is this rule prescribed for a king whose mind is entirely devoted to Śiva.
It is proclaimed that for a Vaiśya there are three baths, while for a Śūdra it is declared to be one;
for all of them, the recitation of mantras is prescribed to be doubled when performed intentionally.
Having bathed, one should indeed drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), each consecrated one hundred times with mantras;
this should be done for three nights, while practicing thus with the thirty-two syllables.
Then, having committed theft, sexual union with another's wife, drinking liquor, and so forth,
one should recite the mantras as before in the previously mentioned locations.
For two years, he remained well-restrained according to the rules known to those who understand vows;
he ate only what was unasked for, ate sparingly, bathed three times a day, and was constantly engaged in meditation.
At the end of two years, the three should go to a sacred field of Śiva;
[this applies] due to harsh speech directed toward the initiating guru, the teacher, or the one who inspires.
From one hundred thousand to one hundred thousand, there is purification by the hundreds; one should arrange it according to a tenth part of that.
[The methods] beginning with the fist-blow (muṣṭighāta) are considered twelvefold when multiplied six times and applied with blood (rakta).
Knowing that purification by means of weapons is a hundredfold more effective, one should not perform it here;
instead, one should perform there a vow according to one's capacity, such as the Kṛcchra or Cāndrāyaṇa penances.
At the conclusion of the vow, one should offer the five products of the cow beginning with water (pañcāmṛta) as in the previous initiation,
and likewise give one's entire possession to the Guru, the Deśika, and the Ācārya.

Purification has been prescribed for four [categories of persons], but there is no purification for one who violates the teacher's bed; likewise, there is none for a preceptor who observes the Śiva-vow, nor for an aspirant (sādhaka), and so forth.
Their purification occurs through the shedding of blood or by reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times;
however, when blood is not seen, even if punishments such as flogging and the like have been administered.
If a practitioner of mantra hears of that [impurity] within half that time, he should pray with sandalwood paste at his feet;
however, if one has eaten food touched by women in their menses unintentionally, [the penance is as follows].
One is purified by ten thousand recitations while fasting; it is not otherwise.
For an act committed intentionally, one is purified by performing a fire-oblation after bathing, provided it is doubled.

Whatever one has eaten or drunk oneself, one should not give it away; however, if it is given through the grace of the Supreme Lord or the gurus, then one should recite [the mantra] eight hundred times.
One who is always pure should offer all cooked food, free from worldly motives, to Śiva;
even if it has been eaten unintentionally during a period of impurity due to death or birth.
Out of desire, one should recite the terrible mantra a thousand times;
likewise, [one should avoid] food from a *gaṇa*, food from a water-jar, and [food from those] fallen from the teaching.
At the parting of the hair ceremony, as well as at the naming ceremony,
and at the time of the first feeding of solid food, one should recite the Sahasrabhakṣita mantra.
Having consumed [the substance] produced from the continuous practice for one year,
beginning from the moment of immediate purification, one should recite the mantra facing south for a period of one thousand [repetitions].
Whether intentionally or unintentionally, from eating the food of a Śūdra even once, the penance is the Bahurūpa for one hundred [repetitions]; for those who are "good Śūdras," it is three hundred.

In a grove of trees, at a pond, a well, or similar sites, in a temple of Śiva, during a wedding, at the ritual release of a bull, and at the gift of cows, one should recite [the mantra] a hundred times.
When meat, scent, or other prohibited substances have been consumed through negligence,
one shall attain purification by reciting the Aghora mantra ten thousand times.
By observing the restraint against sexual intercourse, food, and evil deeds,
one is purified by half of a thousand [repetitions] even when using ointments, drinks, garments, and the like.

If there is a loss of food obtained through alms or a lapse in the practice of sleeping on the ground, purification occurs by [reciting] five hundred [mantras]; likewise, for a lapse in the resolve regarding sleeping on the ground, one should recite the Astra-mantra one hundred times.
But when the affliction caused by planets, spirits, piśācas, and so forth has been severed, one becomes pure by reciting the Ghoramantra three hundred times; it is not otherwise.

Having performed rites for pacification and nourishment out of constraint or affection, purification occurs only after three hundred [breaths] have elapsed; it is not otherwise for one who possesses many forms.
The expiation for those established in the Śiva-dharma has been declared,
as well as for those established in the worldly dharma (loka-dharma) when a death-impurity occurs or when worship is performed.
Having prescribed the expiation accompanied by the internal sacrifice (mantaryāga), it must be performed with a sacrificial fee of one thousand [cows]; it shall not be otherwise.
Having performed rites such as *uccāṭana* (driving away) and others, being pure and endowed with many forms,
one should never, under any circumstances, cause the act of killing (*māraṇa*) to be done by means of a mantra or even mentally.
O King, having performed the installation and initiation in the three sacred sites and so forth,
one who is pure should perform ten thousand recitations of the Aghora mantra while abstaining from food.
A leather strap made of hemp, wool, linen, or muñja grass shall be used as a binding;
likewise, a leather water-container may be carried wherever it is obtained.
One should likewise recite three hundred times the mantra of Bahurūpin;
and [one should avoid] milk, curd, ghee, honey, meat, and so forth.
One should recite the mantra of Bahurūpa three hundred times over salt, oil, pungent substances, and various perfumes; thereby one shall attain purification.
Silver, gems, gold, lapis lazuli, pearls,
as well as a village, a bull, an elephant, a woman, cattle, and other things, a man [should offer].
Having diligently purified the various forms within the Āsaya and other locations,
one should construct a monastery or a private residence and recite the Aghora mantra one hundred thousand times.
Even for those who have committed many sins, when Śaṅkara has appeared before them,
they shall attain perfection after reciting the thirty-two syllable mantra.

In this regard, from the defect of Śaṅkara, as well as from the mixing of vessels (bhāṇḍa-śaṅkara), there are three hundred [faults] of Aghora; from Śaṅkara, there are twenty-two thousand and so forth.
One becomes pure by sweeping away hundreds of pieces of wood, stones, grass, and the like;
likewise, O skillful one, one is purified even when killing living beings, provided they have already been killed by others.
One should recite [the mantra] one hundred times over an unborn creature, half that number (fifty) over a goat out of desire;
one hundred times over a donkey, and one thousand times over a cat.

For killing a dog or a jackal, the penance is doubled; for a monkey or a cock, it is likewise; and for killing snakes or other egg-born creatures such as swans and the like, O Śakra, one remains [in that state].
For killing deer such as lions and the like, or for slaughtering small animals such as goats and the like,
one becomes pure by performing the Śatātanu penance a hundred times, or by the Bahurūpa penance a hundred times.
If, through negligence, one is struck by a dog, a jackal, or a serpent,
one should bathe in the midst of cool water and recite the Aghora mantra one thousand times.
Having performed a bath with his clothes on for the third [offense], he becomes pure after a hundred [repetitions];
likewise upon touching the left side [of the body] or upon seeing a bad dream.
Due to the contemplation of misfortune and the speaking of falsehood,
whether by deed, mind, or speech, one should recite the *hṛdaya* mantra a thousand times.
If semen or the like is discharged while one is sleeping unintentionally,
one should bathe, wear fresh clothes, and recite the Astra-mantra one hundred times.
For causing an abortion through lust, one should recite the third [mantra] ten thousand times;
having killed a cow through negligence, one becomes pure by reciting the Aghora [mantra] one hundred thousand times.
By giving a hundred cows, or even a hundred thousand, one is purified;
but having eaten at a Śūdra's house, one becomes pure by eating [at such places] a thousand times, provided it was done intentionally.
One should conduct oneself toward practitioners and others through both deed and mind in such a way that some degree of world-weariness arises.
Having first observed a three-night fast and being purified, he who— endowed with the thirty-two syllables—
should void excrement or even utter a mantra in a temple [is blessed].
In a temple of the gods, at Rāma, and especially in a sacred field of Śiva,
one who is pure and free from desire should recite [the mantra] one thousand times for each quarter-verse.
Having intentionally or even unintentionally killed a Śūdra child,
one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times in sequence, or half of that if it was not intentional.
For one who has not yet attained full authority, he shall indeed remain a twice-born for ten days;
for a king, it is twelve days, and for a Vaiśya, fifteen days.
However, the [period of impurity] for Śūdras lasts for one month regarding obligatory rites and the like, and not otherwise;
but for those initiated into Nirvāṇa, no birth-impurity exists at all.
For them, there exists the birth-impurity (sūtaka) according to worldly custom;
yet, since there is no cutting of the top-knot (śikhāccheda) therein, that initiation is considered merely worldly.
The internal sacrifice (antaryāga) must be performed by those who are initiated according to worldly [rites];
likewise, recitations (japa), circumambulations (pradakṣiṇa), and so forth, should be performed with great effort.
A celibate student (brahmacārī) is never eligible to eat the food of a householder;
however, for forest-dwellers (vānaprastha) and ascetics (yatī), one should recite the mantra as before while facing south.
Likewise, having eaten the food of those who bear other sectarian marks (liṅgin), one should recite the *dakṣiṇa* [mantra] a thousand times;
for the twice-born, such a recitation is prescribed as a fast (*upavāsa*).
He who, out of delusion, speaks a false oath before the feet of his guru,
and another wicked-souled person who administers it— both of them shall go to hell.
In all cases of commingling, the *aghora* mantra is to be recited as the cause for the purification of the mind, until the mind becomes serene.
Through the practice of recitation (japa), fasting at sacred fords (tīrtha), and association with the abodes of Śiva;
through the offering of water-pots (gaḍḍuka) and the pouring of sesame seeds and clarified butter.
By being in the presence of the teacher and by hearing the Saṃhitā,
[the sins committed] against gods, twice-born men, cows, and Śiva are not [present] in the five [elements] nor in the sky.
Just as the sun shines when released from the clouds, so does he shine resplendent in the world.
"Therefore, one should perform penance today for the sake of livelihood.
Thus ends the general procedure for penance called Āgneya in the Mahātantras of this lineage. 44.
Know that the *liṅga* is threefold: manifest (*vyakta*), devoted (*bhakta*), and fearful (*bhaya*).
Regarding the rule for expiation, one should not speak of the distinctions between these types of *liṅgas*.
O child, Śiva alone abides as three according to the distinction of the principles;
therefore, listen now to the classification of the liṅgas regarding the rules for expiation.
Having established Yāgeśvara and whatever else is situated there, one should prescribe the ritual procedure or the offering of oblations (bali).
One should personally perform the purification of transgressions before one's own chosen liṅga.
When an offense has been committed by others, purification is prescribed therein;
by means of one's own chosen *liṅga*, the practitioner effects the purification of both here.
In the ritual procedure, offenses are to be known as those committed by oneself and those committed by others;
each of these is further to be understood as being of two kinds, distinguished by whether they are intentional or unintentional.
That [initiation] should also be known to be of two kinds: the elemental (bhautika) and the final (naiṣṭhika).
The elemental is considered to be fourfold, according to the distinctions of the pledges (samaya) and so forth.
Furthermore, purification through the infliction of suffering upon others is described as *liṅga*.
For one who is unstable and must be established [in the path], or for one who is both unstable and established, the purification is twofold.

O child, one should calculate twice the [measure] for a movable [object] already established on the head, and four times for a fixed [object]; first, one should prescribe the purification of the purification.
The common [purification] as well as that which is to be accomplished is declared to be twofold;
however, for that known as duality-and-non-duality, one should prescribe a purification that is twice [as much].
However, that common purification is considered to be doubled when [the offense] occurs without them,
provided that the transgression against one's own chosen *liṅga* was committed by others.
They declare that for an offense committed intentionally, the penance for purification should be doubled;
this applies whether one acts without desire or with desire, and whether it is done by oneself or by another.
Having understood [the nature of the offense] again and again, Śikhidhvaja should perform the expiation;
for one initiated by a practitioner, purification is considered to be twofold.
For students of sacred knowledge (brahmacārins), purification from material contact is considered to be twofold;
for those outside the [four] castes who have been seen with [impure] signs, purification is prescribed.
In the same way, there is the purification of his three marks.
Likewise, listen now to the purification for his cold [discharge];
the group consists of the four castes, and in the drama, there is another, the *varttaka*.
The second [type] is considered that for which purity occurs through contact with one's own group;
the third is that for which bathing is required upon contact with those of the crow-caste and similar groups.
