The fourth, however, is the dog-outcaste (śvapavādin), because he touches one's clothes;
O child, seeing him or touching him is avoided by those who seek the four goals of human life.
Furthermore, the measure of the faults residing in the *liṅga* is now declared;
upon the mere occurrence of which a man becomes liable to perform expiation (*prāyaścitta*).
The atonement should be known as prescribed by the ancients; one must not step over the shadow of the Liṅga.
Purification occurs through the Aghora mantra performed a hundred times, and not otherwise.
Purification is required for a thousand [transgressions] when [the linga] is overturned; it is double that amount for turning it over twice;
and for three or four times overturning the linga upon the surface of the earth.
If it is struck by lightning once, it is pure; if struck twice, it is pure up to one hundred thousand [miles]. But when a strike occurs, one should declare it pure up to twenty thousand [miles].
If one does not go even ten thousand [steps] from a distance, one remains pure;
however, upon touching or stepping over [the corpse], one should declare purification after twenty thousand steps.

O Guha, purification occurs upon touching the dust of a quarter [of the footprint] from half [the distance]; it is not otherwise. But if a minute [particle] is seen, there is purification by two blades of grass and by that water.
In the Sūtra and Sūtrodaka, one becomes pure after half a *lakṣa* [of recitations] or at the quarter-mark;
however, due to contact with a woman with menstrual blood, purification is ordained after half a *lakṣa*.

By touching water that has come into contact with that [feces], one becomes pure after three-quarters of the time as before; likewise, by touching feces, one becomes pure after three-quarters of a *lakṣa* [of breaths] through that same water.
Likewise, one should declare purification for falling into a pit containing discarded flower offerings;
and from falling into a pit of excrement, one is considered pure after half a lakh [of recitations].
Purification occurs through the rubbing of a stable image with a *lakṣa* [of ashes] and likewise through its re-installation;
even one situated between the emergence [of the deity] and [the end of the rite] is purified by those [acts] excluding the *samudgaka*.

If the *liṅga* falls due to negligence while being carried in the *samuṅgaka* (a type of carrying-pole), one should perform fifty thousand repetitions with the hand; the ritual duration may then be slightly less or more than a full *kalpa*.
But when [the vessel] is devoid of the *samudraka* and has fallen from the hand, O Śivā,
purification is achieved by the previously mentioned measure of one cubit doubled.
If beauty is lost even when not licked by ten thousand [bees],
then purity is seen only when that which lacks beauty has been abandoned by others.
When [the water] is defiled, its color altered, or its path changed; when drunk from the interior of a river or similar source;
or when it has been taken away, lost, or dropped through negligence into a great vessel.

If the sacrificial animal has been licked by a dog or a crow, or if it is impure, or if it is stolen at night by thieves, or if it is lost with only its value remaining; [in these cases, one should perform the following].
When both opposing groups are touched, renunciation is prescribed;
one should diligently recite the mantra one hundred thousand times and then re-establish that form.
Then the practitioner, having burnt away his sins, attains purity;
otherwise, they are not liberated because of the occurrence of various [karmic] alternatives.
In this manner, one should perform the expiation for the rosary;
therein, one should prescribe purification according to the previously mentioned quarter-verse on the linga.
In cases of transgressions regarding breath control (prāṇāyāma), a penance equal to one-eighth of that for the linga should be prescribed by the Guru who knows the reality.
When those belonging to the four castes, beginning with the Brāhmaṇas, who have not received Śiva-initiation (śivadīkṣā),
ask about their own chosen liṅga, one should prescribe the appropriate expiation (prāyaścitta).

If one who is pure is touched by members of the fisherman (kaivarta) caste out of negligence while they are holding their own chosen lingas, the purification requires one hundred, two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, or five hundred repetitions [of the mantra] for the twice-born and other castes respectively.
The practitioner attains purification after ten thousand [repetitions], and not otherwise, O subtle one;
when touched by flocks of crows and the like, a man is purified after thirty thousand.
When [the sun] is seen by Rākṣasas and others, one is purified by ten thousand arrows;
when touched by the four classes [of beings], one becomes pure through the mere sight of that which is devoid of qualities.
When the *liṅga* is touched by those initiated into their own stream (*svaśrota*), it incurs no fault;
however, if the *liṅga* is touched through negligence by those who follow the left or right paths (*vāmamārga* and *dakṣiṇamārga*), [there is a transgression].
The mantra-practitioner is purified by ten thousand [recitations] through the great ablution (mahāsnāna), and not otherwise;
one should also completely avoid contact with those of the left-hand and right-hand paths.
Purification from contact occurs by means of a hundred [repetitions] of meditative cultivation for those who have increased their duality;
however, one should avoid contact with those who are burdened by the five great sins.
Purification from speaking with [an impure person] is considered to be ten thousand times [the standard], while from touching them it is double that;
from sharing a bed it is one hundred thousand, and from eating [with them] one is pure after one million.
[One should avoid] contact with Buddhists and Cārvākas, those who delight in reviling Śiva,
those who defile the scriptures, and especially those who are outcastes (patita).

Contact with them should be avoided with great effort; one becomes pure by avoiding contact for two hundred [instants]. One must strictly avoid touching those who belong to the Kaulika and Pālika [sects].
One should never engage in disputes with those who are blind, deaf, or one-eyed;
likewise, one should avoid living together with them or even touching them from afar.
Likewise, those noble followers of the Sāṃkhya school who believe in the pre-existence of the effect and are greedy for its attainment should not engage in disputes at all.
One should avoid the company of the Digambaras and the Śvetapaṭas; likewise, one should avoid speaking with those who are heretics.
But that deluded soul who forms an association with the path of those who avoid [the virtuous] will not go to the city of Śiva, even if he has performed great penance.
If no formal accusation is made, there shall never be a dispute;
even one who acts thus with a deluded mind shall obtain purification after ten thousand [repetitions].
Where there are indeed one hundred thousand verses, there is a greater observance;
that is the "Great Bath" (mahāsnāna), while the "Great Worship" (mahāpūjā) is performed according to the quarter [of the text].
A great ablution (mahāsnāna) should be performed using two thousand palas of milk, curd, ghee, and so forth, combined with the "great triphalā."
One should likewise arrange before Śiva the *kallola* species, the *punnāga*, and the *śrīphala*, as well as the *mahāvarti*, the *tadvāvarti*, and the *tadvādatva*.
The great bath (mahāsnāna) is declared to consist of [the image] joined with red wicks and endowed with divine fragrance; the great worship (mahāpūjā) is half of that.
Two fasts should always be observed for ten thousand [recitations]:
one-tenth of the total from the recitation (*japa*), and one-twentieth from the *gaḍḍuka* vessel.
Truthfulness, the vow of celibacy, eating on the ground, eating only at night,
the renunciation of oil-baths, truthful speech, and abstaining from food containing meat or honey.
One skilled in the scriptures should perform [the rite] until the conclusion of the recitation;
indeed, one incurs the penance of consuming the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), which is beneficial.
One should worship the guide in due order with land, jewels, drinks, and garments;
for if a transgression occurs, it would lead to the destruction of the performer.
Furthermore, other things that are requested should be performed by the Guru twice as much as previously stated;
however, O wise one, he must never perform anything that was not requested.
One should worship [the deity] like Śiva, but one must honor the Guru in the teaching of Śiva;
[this applies even to those who are] children, women, the elderly, those addicted to worldly enjoyments, or those afflicted by disease.
However, for women and artisans, there exists no expiation; therefore, the Nirbījika initiation should be performed for them, and no other.
Devotion to the conduct of the observance (samayācāra) is considered initiation itself that bestows liberation;
yet that initiation is independent, and that vision is conjoined with the seed-syllable.
For those who possess desire and seek the goal of the *samaya*, even among the teachers, women are like the two *vasus*; they are always devoted to the worship of the *liṅga* with devotion.
When a transgression has occurred, one should cause the penance to be administered;
their purification by means of that penance is as previously stated for one quarter.
Due to incapacity, the manifest [deity] is to be worshipped by the *samayin*, the *putraka*, and others;
or, while remaining in one's own boat, it may be worshipped or not worshipped with sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*).
One's own guru should be appointed to the tasks of worship, recitation, and so forth;
one's own guru is to be honored like Śiva, as are brothers, disciples, teachers, and others.
The practitioners (sādhakas) are declared by the Lord to be like sons; those who abide by the covenant (samaya) are to be regarded like brothers and like Śiva himself by one who desires Śiva.
The preceptors should be employed for rites such as pacification, especially in the rite of consecration;
likewise, practitioners should be employed for purification, according to their respective dispositions.
Whether one's own or another's, those to be employed in the worship of Suśiva—
be they *samayins* or *putrakas*— must not eat without having performed the worship.
When a birth-impurity (sūtaka) occurs, the deity must first be worshipped by the householder;
he may then associate with one who is impure from birth, but not otherwise.
Or, if one's own food is unavailable, then food belonging to another may be used for worship;
having recited over food from a house of impurity (sūtaka) according to the authority of the Tantras, one who is in a state of impurity (sūtakī) may proceed.
The internal sacrifice (antaryāga) must be performed during the period of birth-impurity; otherwise, one is not pure.
One should bow down and praise the Supreme Lord with songs and hymns.
When the cutting of the crest-lock (*śikhā*) has been performed, he says that [the soul] is joined to the Power (*Śakti*) by means of the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*),
according to the measure of the six paths (*ṣaḍadhvan*) and through the movement of the sixfold categories.
For them, the impurity of birth or death does not apply; they are fit for the worship of Śiva.
At the time of the deity’s worship, if drops fall upon the body [of the officiant],
then an expiation must be performed according to the sequence of the rules.
The mantrin should, according to the rule, contemplate Sadyojāta sevenfold from the feet up to the knees; he is purified, and not otherwise at any time.
One should meditate on the limbs of the Brahmins from the knees down to the private parts;
one should recite the Kalā-mantra twenty-one times, and no other mantra.
One should likewise meditate on the multiform [deity] from the secret place to the heart;
one should recite the kalā-mantra twenty-one times, and no other.
One should likewise contemplate the multiform [deity] from the secret place to the end of the heart;
if it is sprinkled from the heart to the top of the head, one should perform the ritual bath.
The recitation of the *Īśāna* mantra one hundred times brings about purification, and not otherwise;
this applies even to one who, being ignorant and acting unintentionally, should consume the remains of the offering (*nirmālya*) after the ritual assembly.
Its purification occurs by means of ten million [repetitions]; for the remaining three [cases], it is as before.
As for the teacher’s property that has been consumed intentionally, [the same applies].
A materialist becomes pure by reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times; the rest is as before.
If the substance of the deity or the guru has been consumed unintentionally:
An ordinary person becomes pure by reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times; the others are as before.
That which has been touched by the remains of offerings (nirmālya), or by a man from the secret parts, [is not purified].
If one consumes even three-quarters [of the forbidden substance] through negligence, that person must perform penance;
if the consumption occurs through negligence, the penance is equal [to the full amount], but if it occurs through indifference, it is half of that.
O Gurudeva, one should protect the property of the twice-born with great care;
for he who, out of negligence, worships non-duality within a dualistic symbol.
Even for the three [classes of practitioners], the recitation of one hundred thousand times should be performed without desire, as before;
thus indeed, one should avoid the mantra of Dvaita with those who lack proper conduct.
When the vessel of a person belonging to one of the [four] castes is free from attachment,
one becomes pure after two hundred, five hundred, and then half of that [two hundred] respectively.
They declare that on a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), a sacrificial post, a palm leaf, or the fire, the penance is double;
however, one should prescribe a penance for a vessel from which the food has not been formally dismissed.
If one who is tranquil should, through negligence, let the Śiva-fire go out,
then purification occurs by reciting the Aghora mantra ten thousand times, and not otherwise.
In the presence of a Śeṣa-liṅga, the recitation of mantras should especially be performed with double the usual number;
furthermore, one becomes pure immediately upon seeing offerings such as insects or meat.
Through the offering of meat out of negligence, one becomes joined with many forms; O limb of life, one is pure through incense, yet one should transform the fifth [element] into a hundred breaths.
In the event of a vessel being struck, two hundred [recitations] of the *Dakṣiṇāmūrti* mantra should be performed by three,
five, seven, or ten masters who have reached the further shore.
One should cause the expiation to be administered by those who are well-versed in their own scriptures and free from excessive greed;
not by fools, nor by procrastinators, nor by atheists, nor by those who rely on mere sophistry.

Just as it has been taught in the scriptures, [the ritual] must be performed neither deficient nor excessive in any respect; by performing it with deficiency or excess, the preceptor shall go to hell.
Therefore, with every effort, one should practice exactly as it has been stated.
Thus ends the chapter on expiation (*prāyaścitta*) in the *Vāthula Mahātantra*. 45.
The wise have declared that there is a combination [of penances] according to the sequence of the statements on expiation;
having extracted this from the scriptures, I too have spoken likewise, yet only the essence in brief.
The virtuous have compiled numerous essential summaries after refining [the teachings] in many ways;
if you have composed works on those, then our composition is likewise [valid].
Born in the lineage of Mattamayūra, there was a sage renowned throughout the earth by the name Śrī Raṇipadralambakarṇa;
he was purified by the refinement of his ears through the study of the entirety of the Śaiva Siddhānta.
Śaṃkara, whose matted locks are marked by the moon, resides on Kailāsa.
From the hermitage of Śrī Raṇipadra, he went to the monastery of Gorāṭika;
there the king favored him with the title "Sīyaka of Dhārā."
In his lineage there was a sage named Śrī Īśvaraśiva, whose lotus-feet were worshipped by kings who were lords of the earth.
His disciple was the sage Śrī Hṛdayaśiva, whose fame equaled that of the Lords of Knowledge (Vidyeśvaras), and who was a stainless mirror for the meaning of all the Āgamas.
The power of whose asceticism rises loftily in all directions, extolled by virtuous people throughout the world;
who effortlessly extracted the essence of the scriptural traditions and instantly scratched away the itching of the arguments of heretics.
Thus was this composed, wherein all enemies were struck down by the collision of many millions of battles.
The *Prāyaścittasamuccaya* is thus completed. || 46 ||
